subject: Banking
title: The First Coins in History
description: A quick win: understand The First Coins in History.

hook.text: Around 600 BC, Lydia in modern Turkey stamped lumps of electrum into standardized coins. Trade changed forever.

buildup.text: Before coins, merchants weighed raw metal for each sale. Stamped coins guaranteed weight and purity instantly.

discovery.text: Standardization was the breakthrough. A coin's stamp said: this weight is verified by the king. Trust was built in.

twist.text: Kings quickly learned to debase coins. Mixing cheap metals into gold coins funded wars but destroyed trust.

climax.text: Coins showed that payment systems need both standardization and honest issuers. Debasement is ancient inflation.

punchline.text: First coins, first inflation tricks. Nothing about money is new.

quiz.question: What was the key innovation of Lydian coins?
options: Stamped standardization guaranteed weight and purity
